analysis.note: Śaṅkara glosses vāyuḥ as prāṇa, the breath of the dying speaker.
Object of the supplied pratipadyatām; in the bhāṣya this is the adhidaivata/sūtrātman, not merely ordinary air.
Masculine accusative singular adjective agreeing with anilam.
In sandhi with following idam: atha + idam → athedaṃ.
Initial i is absorbed in athedaṃ; nominative with śarīram as subject of supplied bhūyāt.
Predicate nominative with śarīram: ‘ending in ashes’.

verification.detail: compound stem bhasmānta as Napumsaka/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Subject of the supplied optative bhūyāt in the bhāṣya.
The bhāṣya takes oṃ as the symbol through which Brahman called Agni is invoked.

verification.detail: avyaya not in kosha or MW

analysis.note: Vocative; glossed by Śaṅkara as saṅkalpātmaka and identified in explanation with Agni.
Second-person singular imperative addressed to kratu/Agni.
Past passive participial stem from √kṛ, used substantively as the object of smara: ‘what has been done’.
Second-person singular imperative; the object is kṛtam.
Repeated vocative; the bhāṣya says the repetition is for ādara, reverent insistence.
Repeated object of smara; the bhāṣya glosses it as karma performed by the speaker.
Fourth occurrence of the second-person singular imperative.

justifications.decision: The opening is not a bare juxtaposition ‘wind, air, immortal’; it is an elliptical wish at death. I translate it as the dying speaker’s breath attaining the immortal Anila after giving up its individual limitation.
options_considered: ordinary wind goes to ordinary air
the wind-god reaches another deity without reference to the dying person
the dying speaker’s prāṇa attains the immortal Anila/sūtrātman
justifications.chosen: vāyuḥ is the speaker’s prāṇa; anilam amṛtam is the immortal cosmic Air/sūtrātman; an optative sense ‘may attain’ is supplied.

evidence.quote: athedānīṃ mama mariṣyato vāyuḥ prāṇo 'dhyātmaparicchedaṃ hitvādhidaivatātmānaṃ sarvātmakamanilamamṛtaṃ sūtrātmānaṃ pratipadyatāmiti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
evidence.translation: ‘Now, of me as I am dying, vāyu—the breath—having abandoned its individual limitation, may attain the immortal Anila, the adhidaivata self, the all-self, the sūtrātman’: this is the completion of the sentence.

justifications.decision: I include this in brackets in the translation because the commentator explicitly says it is to be understood, while distinguishing it from the gross body that becomes ash.
options_considered: do not translate any implicit subtle-body departure
identify idaṃ śarīram only with the subtle body
understand a separate implicit liṅga-departure clause, then the gross body’s becoming ash
justifications.chosen: An implicit clause is understood: the subtle body (liṅga), shaped by knowledge and action, departs.

evidence.translation: And this subtle body, conditioned by knowledge and action, should be understood as departing, because of the force of the request for a path.
Then may this body, offered in the fire, come to have ashes as its end.

justifications.decision: bhasmāntam is construed as a bahuvrīhi predicate adjective, not as an accusative object or a mere appositional noun.
options_considered: ‘this ash-ended body’ as an accusative phrase
‘this body is ashes’ without supplied verb
‘may this body, offered into fire, end in ashes’
justifications.chosen: idaṃ bhasmāntaṃ śarīram is a nominative optative sentence: ‘may this body become ash-ending’.

evidence.translation: Then may this body, offered in the fire, come to have ashes as its end.

justifications.decision: I leave Om as Om in the translation but gloss it as the symbol of Brahman called Agni, since the bhāṣya does not treat it as a mere exclamation.
options_considered: a meaningless or merely auspicious particle
the sacred syllable without further reference
the oṃ-symbol of Brahman called Agni
justifications.chosen: oṃ invokes Brahman called Agni through the oṃ-symbol.

evidence.translation: ‘Om’—according to the meditation, because it has oṃ as its symbol, truth-natured Brahman called Agni is spoken of as non-different [from it].

justifications.decision: The translation ‘O Agni-as-Resolve (kratu)’ follows Śaṅkara’s saṅkalpātmaka gloss and his explicit agne in explaining kṛtaṃ smara.
options_considered: O sacrifice
O intellect/mind without Agni-reference
O Agni as resolve/will
justifications.chosen: krato is a vocative to Agni as resolve/will, not ‘sacrifice’.

evidence.quote: he krato! saṅkalpātmaka! smara yanmama smartavyaṃ tasya kālo 'yaṃ pratyupasthito 'taḥ smara /
evidence.translation: O kratu! O one whose nature is resolve! Remember what is to be remembered for me; the time for it has now arrived, therefore remember.

evidence.quote: etāvantaṃ kālaṃ bhāvitaṃ kṛtamagne smara yanmayā bālyaprabhṛtyanuṣṭhitaṃ karma tacca smara /
evidence.translation: Remember, O Agni, what has been done and cultivated for all this time—the action performed by me from childhood onward; remember that too.

justifications.decision: I translate kṛtaṃ smara as ‘remember what has been done’, with kṛtam as a substantive neuter accusative object of smara.
options_considered: kṛtam as a finite verb
kṛtam as a vague adjective ‘made’ without object force
kṛtam as the performed karma to be remembered by Agni
justifications.chosen: kṛtam means the action/deed performed by the speaker, especially from childhood onward.

evidence.quote: etāvantaṃ kālaṃ bhāvitaṃ kṛtamagne smara yanmayā bālyaprabhṛtyanuṣṭhitaṃ karma tacca smara /
evidence.translation: Remember, O Agni, what has been done and cultivated for all this time—the action performed by me from childhood onward; remember that too.

justifications.decision: I do not collapse the repeated words into a single command, because the bhāṣya states that the repetition is for ādara.
options_considered: treat the repetition as accidental
translate only one occurrence
preserve the repetition as deliberate reverent insistence
justifications.chosen: The repetition krato smara kṛtaṃ smara is retained as reverent insistence.

evidence.translation: The repetition ‘O kratu, remember; remember what has been done’ is for the sake of reverence/earnest regard.

translation: May my breath (vāyu), as I am dying, leaving its individual limitation, attain the immortal cosmic Air (anila); [may this subtle body (liṅga), shaped by knowledge and action, depart.] Then may this body, consigned to fire, end in ashes. Om—the symbol of Brahman called Agni. O Agni-as-Resolve (kratu), remember; remember what has been done. O Agni-as-Resolve, remember; remember what has been done.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render vāyu and anila as two ordinary ‘winds’, missing Śaṅkara’s prāṇa → immortal sūtrātman/adhidaivata construal at the moment of death.
It might omit the implicit departure of the subtle body (liṅga), which Śaṅkara says must be understood because the next mantra asks for a path.
It might take idaṃ bhasmāntaṃ śarīram as an accusative phrase; the bhāṣya supplies bhūyāt and makes it ‘may this body end in ashes’.
It might translate kratu as ‘sacrifice’ or generic ‘mind’; Śaṅkara glosses it as saṅkalpātmaka and explains the addressee as Agni.
It might smooth away the repeated smara phrases, while the bhāṣya explicitly says the repetition is for ādara, reverent emphasis.
analyzer_disagreements: amṛtam: ByT5 tagged it as neuter accusative; I analyze it as masculine accusative singular, agreeing with masculine anilam, because Śaṅkara construes anilam amṛtam as a single accusative object (line 1).

idam, bhasmāntam, and śarīram: ByT5 tagged the forms as neuter accusative; I analyze them as neuter nominative singular, since Śaṅkara supplies bhūyāt and makes idaṃ śarīram the subject and bhasmāntam the predicate (line 3).
bhasmāntam: ByT5 split bhasma + antam; I analyze the whole inflected form as the bahuvrīhi compound stem bhasmānta, ‘having ashes as its end’, predicated of śarīram (line 3).

kṛtam, both occurrences: ByT5 lemmatizes to the verbal root kṛ/participle; I record the nominal participial stem kṛta as a neuter accusative singular substantive, because Śaṅkara glosses it with anuṣṭhitaṃ karma, the action performed (line 6).
mula: vāyur anilam amṛtam athedaṃ bhasmāntaṃ śarīram | oṃ krato smara kṛtaṃ smara krato smara kṛtaṃ smara
